lines.sub: Back to the main allowance result: why did EndorseRank not beat the plain count? Let's look at it with a formula.
lines.tts: Back to the main allowance result. Why did EndorseRank not beat the plain count? Let's look at it with a formula.

lines.sub: Here is the small world from chapter 4 again.
lines.tts: Here is the small world from chapter four again.

lines.sub: The water in each cup is the share of a long walk that stays at each node.
lines.tts: The water in each cup is the share of a long walk that stays at each node.

lines.sub: On the right, we'll build a closed form step by step: a formula that gives the score directly.
lines.tts: On the right, we'll build a closed form step by step, a formula that gives the score directly.

card.title: Closed form
card.body: A direct formula for the score, here only for depth-one spenders

lines.sub: First, c: the share every node receives equally at every step.
lines.tts: First, c, the share every node receives equally at every step.

lines.sub: It is the restart share plus the dangling-node share.
lines.tts: It is the restart share plus the dangling-node share.

lines.sub: A node with no incoming edge, like A, receives only this, so its score is exactly c.
lines.tts: A node with no incoming edge, like A, receives only this, so its score is exactly c.

lines.sub: In the small world, c is 0.15 plus the product of 0.85 and D's cup, 0.4706, with that whole sum divided by 4.
lines.tts: In the small world, c is zero point one five plus the product of zero point eight five and D's cup, zero point four seven zero six, with that whole sum divided by four.

lines.sub: That gives 0.1375, the same as A's cup.
lines.tts: That gives zero point one three seven five, the same as the cup of node A.

lines.sub: The balance equation of every node starts at c and adds the shares that come in along edges.
lines.tts: The balance equation of every node starts at c and adds the shares that come in along edges.

lines.sub: Most spenders, like B and C here, receive approvals only from owners that receive no approvals themselves.
lines.tts: Most spenders, like B and C here, receive approvals only from owners that receive no approvals themselves.

lines.sub: We call such spenders depth-one spenders, as the badges say.
lines.tts: We call such spenders depth-one spenders, as the badges say.

lines.sub: Such an owner's score is c, so in the spender's balance equation we put c in place of the owner's share, r_u.
lines.tts: Such an owner's score is c, so in the spender's balance equation we put c in place of the owner's share, r of u.

lines.sub: Because c is the same for every owner, it comes out of the sum.
lines.tts: Because c is the same for every owner, it comes out of the sum.

lines.sub: That gives c plus the product of c, d and δ, where d is our damping factor.
lines.tts: That gives c plus the product of c, d and delta, where d is our damping factor.

lines.sub: Pulling out the common c leaves a short formula: c times, in brackets, 1 plus the product of d and δ.
lines.tts: Pulling out the common c leaves a short formula, c times, in brackets, one plus the product of d and delta.

lines.sub: δ adds up, over the owners, the piece of each owner's allowance weight that went to this spender.
lines.tts: Delta adds up, over the owners, the piece of each owner's allowance weight that went to this spender.

lines.sub: Let's check the formula with B, whose only owner is A.
lines.tts: Let's check the formula with B, whose only owner is A.

lines.sub: A's arrows carry 2 and 1, so A gave 2 of its total weight of 3 to B, two thirds.
lines.tts: The arrows of node A carry two and one, so A gave two of its total weight of three to B, two thirds.

lines.sub: And that gives 0.2154, exactly B's cup.
lines.tts: And that gives zero point two one five four, exactly B's cup.

lines.sub: C also matches, at 0.1765.
lines.tts: C also matches, at zero point one seven six five.

lines.sub: But for D, marked deeper, the short formula does not hold.
lines.tts: But for D, marked deeper, the short formula does not hold.

lines.sub: D's owners, B and C, receive approvals themselves, so shares that spread one more step come in.
lines.tts: D's owners, B and C, receive approvals themselves, so shares that spread one more step come in.

lines.sub: So D is computed from the full balance equation: 0.4706.
lines.tts: So D is computed from the full balance equation. Zero point four seven zero six.

lines.sub: Here is δ in an example: three owners approved 1, 2 and 4 spenders.
lines.tts: Here is delta in an example. Three owners approved one, two and four spenders.

lines.sub: The plain count is 3.
lines.tts: The plain count is three.

lines.sub: But δ is 1 plus one half plus one quarter: 1.75.
lines.tts: But delta is one plus one half plus one quarter. One point seven five.

lines.sub: You can see the three pieces stacked in the bar.
lines.tts: You can see the three pieces stacked in the bar.

lines.sub: c and d are the same for every depth-one spender, so the order of the scores is the order of δ, whatever d is.
lines.tts: c and d are the same for every depth-one spender, so the order of the scores is the order of delta, whatever d is.

lines.sub: In effect, EndorseRank counts the owners, each divided by the weight of everything that owner approved.
lines.tts: In effect, EndorseRank counts the owners, each divided by the weight of everything that owner approved.

lines.sub: The more spenders an owner approves, the smaller each share, and that is where the order differs from the count.
lines.tts: The more spenders an owner approves, the smaller each share, and that is where the order differs from the count.

lines.sub: For such spenders, apart from that division and the age and value weights, little differs from the count.
lines.tts: For such spenders, apart from that division and the age and value weights, little differs from the count.

lines.sub: There is no information for the walk to add by spreading.
lines.tts: There is no information for the walk to add by spreading.

lines.sub: In the real same-window graph, c is 7.64 × 10⁻⁸.
lines.tts: In the real same-window graph, c is seven point six four times ten to the minus eight.

lines.sub: We checked how well this formula fits on the real graph.
lines.tts: We checked how well this formula fits on the real graph.

lines.sub: The legend at the top shows three kinds of dots.
lines.tts: The legend at the top shows three kinds of dots.

lines.sub: One dot is 10 same-window spenders.
lines.tts: One dot is ten same-window spenders.

lines.sub: Of the 14,406 same-window spenders, 12,039 were depth-one spenders.
lines.tts: Of the fourteen thousand four hundred and six same-window spenders, twelve thousand and thirty-nine were depth-one spenders.

lines.sub: The bright amber dots are depth one; the faint dots and the dots with a rose outline are deeper spenders.
lines.tts: The bright amber dots are depth one. The faint dots and the dots with a rose outline are deeper spenders.

lines.sub: Every single depth-one spender matched the formula to within 1%.
lines.tts: Every single depth-one spender matched the formula to within one percent.

lines.sub: Of the remaining 2,367 deeper spenders, only 26.4% matched.
lines.tts: Of the remaining two thousand three hundred and sixty-seven deeper spenders, only twenty-six point four percent matched.

lines.sub: So shares spreading over several steps really exist.
lines.tts: So shares spreading over several steps really exist.

lines.sub: Over all spenders it is 87.9%, and in W0, 73.7%.
lines.tts: Over all spenders it is eighty-seven point nine percent, and in W zero, seventy-three point seven percent.

lines.sub: Yet even with that spreading, EndorseRank did not beat the plain count.
lines.tts: Yet even with that spreading, EndorseRank did not beat the plain count.

lines.sub: Let's put this next to the transfer side.
lines.tts: Let's put this next to the transfer side.

lines.sub: Below, the four comparisons with the raw degree, the plain count, are gathered on one page.
lines.tts: Below, the four comparisons with the raw degree, the plain count, are gathered on one page.

lines.sub: Right of 0, the walk score did better.
lines.tts: Right of zero, the walk score did better.

lines.sub: On the transfer side, in blue, the walk wins.
lines.tts: On the transfer side, in blue, the walk wins.

lines.sub: On the allowance side, in amber, the count wins.
lines.tts: On the allowance side, in amber, the count wins.

lines.sub: The colored dots are the revised analysis, our main result; the gray markers of the registered analysis point the same way in all four.
lines.tts: The colored dots are the revised analysis, our main result. The gray markers of the registered analysis point the same way in all four.

lines.sub: All four comparisons were computed after the labels were known, so they are post hoc.
lines.tts: All four comparisons were computed after the labels were known, so they are post hoc.
